disclaimer: Everything on this page is a proposal or a judgement unless it is explicitly marked as sourced. No topic here has been written, and none of them is a claim about a product.

There is no keyword-volume data anywhere in this repository, and none was invented for this page. Any statement about what people search for is labelled as judgement and is an argument from the product's own documentation, not a measurement. Publishing estimated search volumes without a measurement tool would be the exact failure this project exists to avoid.

Every article proposed here is buildable from official manufacturer pages and owner's manuals only. None of them requires a hands-on test, and none may claim one: the FTC warns that you cannot talk about your experience with a product you have not tried (S8).
Each row names the official source the finished article would have to cite. If a row's sources cannot support its headline, the headline has to change - not the citation.
demand_note: Demand is argued, not measured. This page has no access to a keyword tool, an Associates reports feed or any analytics. The 'why it could earn traffic' column is reasoning about what a documented product difference answers, and it is labelled as judgement everywhere it appears.

topics.title: Two 3-quart drawers or one 8-quart basket: the only question that matters
topics.hook: Nearly the same total volume. Completely different dinners.

topics.title: What '450F Hi-Fry' actually means - and why the same badge means two different things

channels.verdict: Forbidden. Listed here because the brief asked for 'pricing analysis' and that phrase hides a prohibited feature.

channels_note: CH-2 and CH-5 are not recommendations to weigh; they are clauses in a contract this site has to operate inside. They are listed alongside the real channels because a traffic plan that omits them reads as if they were never considered.

cadence.rhythm: One sourced guide a fortnight, four then re-measure.
cadence.why_this_rhythm: Sequencing is the whole point. Publishing all four working titles at once would produce four unmeasured articles; publishing them in series means the second is chosen with the first's arrival data in hand. Amazon's own application guidance refers to a body of posts and to content being recent, so cadence serves the account as well as search.
definition_of_done: The guide is registered in data/articles.json, which puts it in the sitemap and the RSS feed on the next build - no separate step exists, and none should.
Every factual sentence cites a registered official source.
Nothing is claimed about search volume or popularity.
The disclosure is present above the fold and every outbound product link is marked rel="sponsored" - both enforced by the build, not by a checklist.
